title: Hybrid eviction proxy and atomic fallback hotpatch
author: Hannah Cho
release_notes: Hotfix: prevent race between eviction and circuit state during regional failover. Adds telemetry guard, atomic fallback proxy, and conservative warmup to avoid request blackholes. Backported to release/2026-02.
description:
Motivation: During a recent regional failover exercise we observed a race where node-eviction and circuit-state reconciliation could momentarily route requests to a node that had drained KV cache but still reported healthy. Impact is transient 5xxs and elevated tail latency for affected tenants. This patch introduces a hybrid eviction proxy that performs an atomic check-and-swap on node circuit state (via hardened metadata lease) and a telemetry-driven fallback path so routing switches to a slower but safe route when sensors detect mismatch.

Design summary: 1) EvictionProxy: new lightweight proxy layer in front of the per-region router. It performs an atomic lease read + compare on the node's circuit token before forwarding. If the token is stale relative to KV-drain marker, the proxy triggers an immediate atomic fallback. 2) AtomicFallback: instead of failing requests, we forward them to the regional slowpath (cold-cache variant) and attach a header x-rw-fallback=atomic to aid tracing. 3) TelemetryGuard: a health gating rule that aggregates short-window mismatches between lease state and kv-drain metric and automatically increases fallback sensitivity for the next 60s. 4) Conservative warmup: when a node returns from eviction, it is marked warmup for 30s where batching limits and token-insert rate are capped.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce locally with the failover simulator (script included)
- [x] Add unit tests for EvictionProxy decision logic
- [x] Add integration test for atomic fallback path under KV-drain
- [x] Add TelemetryGuard thresholds with feature flag default on for SRE
- [x] Add console metrics and a debug trace for x-rw-fallback events
- [x] Backport to release/2026-02 and ship hotpatch

Commits (high level):
- feat(eviction): introduce EvictionProxy and lease CAS check (cho/eviction-proxy)
- feat(fallback): add AtomicFallback route and header propagation (cho/fallback)
- perf(warmup): implement conservative warmup throttle configs (cho/warmup)
- test: simulator and integration harness for failover races (cho/tests)
- ci: add canary job gating TelemetryGuard on SRE feature flag (ci/telemetry-canary)

Files changed (high level):
- services/router/eviction_proxy.go (new)
- services/router/fallback_handler.go (new)
- infra/telemetry/guards.go (updated)
- tests/failover/simulator.sh (new)
- config/defaults.yaml (warmup/fallback thresholds)
- docs/runbooks/eviction-fallback.md (new)

Testing and CI: The PR adds a canary pipeline step that runs the simulator against a mini-cluster (local docker compose). CI initially failed on race conditions in the integration harness; I fixed ordering in the simulator and re-ran. All checks passing on the final run (unit/integration/linters). Canary was left enabled behind feature flag 'sre.eviction_atomic_fallback'.

Review thread (highlights):
- Miguel Alvarez: "Can we avoid an extra network hop for hot paths? Concerned about added p50."
  - Author: "EvictionProxy is co-located in the router process (in-process call) not a network hop; microbenchmark shows +1ms p50 at 99th percentile improves overall failure rate. Added note in docs."
- Priya Raman: "What if lease store is partitioned? Could we flip too eagerly?"
  - Author: "TelemetryGuard reduces sensitivity if lease store errors spike; fallback is conservative — we route to a safe slowpath not drop. Added additional metric telemetry."
- Ethan Gold: "Please add explicit span tags for x-rw-fallback to make tracing queries easier."
  - Author: "Done in fallback_handler.go; tag is x-rw-fallback and included in the routing span."

Post-merge actions:
- Toggle feature flag to 'on' for canary regions for 72h, monitor fallback rate and 5xxs (SRE runbook updated).
- Backport already applied to release branch and reconciled with release manager.
- Follow-up: evaluate removing warmup throttle after 2 weeks if no regressions.

Why this is safe: The change keeps the canonical routing logic intact and only adds a guarded check that routes to an existing slowpath. There is no change to token accounting or billing. The warmup throttle is conservative and parameterized via config with defaults matching current observed p99.

Rollout: merged via squash-and-merge after approvals. Release notes and runbook linked.
